h: Jacob Israel and the Work of Refinement

p: "וַיֵּשֶׁב יַעֲקֹב בְּאֶרֶץ מְגוּרֵי אָבִיו וְגוֹמֵר, אֵלֶּה תֹּלְדוֹת יַעֲקֹב יוֹסֵף וְגוֹמֵר" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לז, א–ב).
— And Jacob dwelt in the land of his father's sojournings, etc. These are the generations of Jacob: Joseph, etc. (Genesis 37:1–2).
בִּפְסוּקִים אֵלּוּ נִזְכַּר שְׁתֵּי פְּעָמִים בְּשֵׁם "יַעֲקֹב",
— In these opening verses, the Patriarch is mentioned twice by the name "Jacob",
וְאַחַר זֶה נִזְכַּר שְׁתֵּי פְּעָמִים בְּשֵׁם "יִשְׂרָאֵל":
— and immediately following, he is mentioned twice by the name "Israel":
"וְיִשְׂרָאֵל אָהַב אֶת יוֹסֵף וְגוֹמֵר" (שָׁם פסוק ג),
— "Now Israel loved Joseph, etc.",
"וַיֹּאמֶר יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל יוֹסֵף: הֲלוֹא אַחֶיךָ רֹעִים בִּשְׁכֶם וְגוֹמֵר" (שָׁם פסוק יג).
— "And Israel said unto Joseph: Do not your brothers feed the flock in Shechem? Come, and I will send you unto them, etc."

p: הָעִנְיָן, דְּהִנֵּה יָדוּעַ שֶׁשֵּׁם "יַעֲקֹב" הוּנַח עַל פְּשׁוּטֵי עָם,
— The explanation is: it is known that the name "Jacob" is applied to the ordinary folk,
וְשֵׁם "יִשְׂרָאֵל" יוֹרֶה עַל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים,
— while the name "Israel" designates advanced Torah scholars,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא לג עַמּוּד ב):
— as written in Bava Metzia (33b):
"'הַגֵּד לְעַמִּי פִּשְׁעָם' (יְשַׁעְיָה נח, א) – אֵלּוּ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים וְכוּלֵי, 'וּלְבֵית יַעֲקֹב חַטֹּאתָם' – אֵלּוּ עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ וְכוּלֵי".
— "'Declare unto My people their transgression'—these are Torah scholars; 'and to the house of Jacob their sins'—these are the unlearned folk."
וְזֶה עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְעַתָּה כֹּה אָמַר ה' בֹּרַאֲךָ יַעֲקֹב וְיֹצֶרְךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל" (שָׁם מג, א):
— And this illuminates the verse: "But now thus says Hashem that created you, O Jacob, and He that formed you, O Israel":
שֶׁיָּדוּעַ שֶׁבְּרִיאָה בְּחִינָה עֶלְיוֹנָה נֶגֶד בְּחִינַת יְצִירָה,
— for it is known that the World of Creation (Beriah) is a higher realm than the World of Formation (Yetzirah),
וּמִשָּׁם נְשָׁמָה וְרוּחַ שֶׁבָּאָדָם:
— and from these realms issue the Neshamah and the Ruach within man:
הַנְּשָׁמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ,
— the Neshamah residing in the brain,
וְעָלֶיהָ נֶאֱמַר: "נְשָׁמָה שֶׁנָּתַתָּ בִּי טְהוֹרָה הִיא" (בְּרָכוֹת ס עַמּוּד ב),
— concerning which we pray: "the soul which You placed within me is pure",
שֶׁהִיא מֵעוֹלַם הַבְּרִיאָה שֶׁכִּמְעַט כֻּלּוֹ טוֹב;
— emanating from the World of Beriah which is almost entirely good;
וּמִשְׁכַּן הָרוּחַ בַּלֵּב שֶׁהוּא מֵעוֹלַם הַיְצִירָה,
— whereas the seat of the Ruach is in the heart, deriving from the World of Yetzirah,
שֶׁשָּׁם מַתְחִיל בְּחִינַת עֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע,
— wherein begins the dichotomy of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil,
וּבַלֵּב מִשְׁכַּן הַיֵּצֶר טוֹב וְהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע:
— and within the heart reside the good inclination and the evil inclination:
בְּ"לֵב חָכָם לִימִינוֹ וְלֵב כְּסִיל לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ" (קֹהֶלֶת י, ב),
— in "a wise man's heart is at his right hand, but a fool's heart is at his left",
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יוּכַל לִפְעָמִים לְהַגִּיעַ אֵיזוֹ פְּגָם גַּם לְהַנְּשָׁמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ.
— and through turbulence in the heart, subtle blemish can sometimes reach even the soul in the brain.
וּלְזֶה יְכַנֶּה הַכָּתוּב שֵׁם "יַעֲקֹב" עַל בְּרִיאָה,
— Therefore Scripture couples the name "Jacob" with Creation (Beriah),
שֶׁהַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ שֶׁל עוֹלַם הַבְּרִיאָה – כָּל כְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
— for in the pristine root of Beriah, all of collective Israel possess a share in the World to Come,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים לְעוֹלָם יִירְשׁוּ אָרֶץ" (יְשַׁעְיָה ס, כא);
— as it is written: "Your people are all righteous, they shall inherit the land forever";
וְשֵׁם "יִשְׂרָאֵל" גַּם עַל יְצִירָה, שֶׁהוּא מְקוֹם הַבְּחִירָה בַּטּוֹב וְהֵיפֶךְ,
— and the name "Israel" upon Formation (Yetzirah), the battleground of free choice between good and evil,
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּכֹחַ תּוֹרָתָם לְהִתְגַּבֵּר עַל יִצְרָם,
— because through the power of their Torah they are equipped to overcome their inclination;
כִּי עַל זֶה יוֹרֶה שֵׁם "יִשְׂרָאֵל": עַל שֵׁם "כִּי שָׂרִיתָ עִם אֱלֹהִים וְעִם אֲנָשִׁים וַתּוּכָל",
— for this is the very definition of "Israel": "for you have striven with divine beings and with men, and have prevailed",
וְהַיְינוּ עִם הַמַּלְאָךְ שֶׁהוּא מִבְּחִינַת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע.
— striving with Samael, the angelic force of the yetzer hara.

paragraphs.text: Bava Metzia 33b: “In the phrase ‘declare to My people their transgression,’ these people are the Torah scholars, whose unwitting transgressions become for them tantamount to intentional transgressions. Due to their erudition, they are held to a higher standard. ‘And to the house of Jacob their sins,’ these are the ignoramuses, whose intentional transgressions become for them tantamount to unwitting transgressions. Due to their lack of erudition, they are held to a lower standard. And that is the basis of that which we learned in a mishna (Avot 4:13), that Rabbi Yehuda says: Be careful in the study of the Talmud, as a transgression based on an unwitting misinterpretation of the Talmud is considered an intentional transgression.”

p: וְהִנֵּה נֶאֱמַר: "וַיֵּשֶׁב יַעֲקֹב בְּאֶרֶץ מְגוּרֵי אָבִיו",
— Now it is written: "And Jacob dwelt in the land of his father's sojournings",
וְאָמְרוּ (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה פד, ג):
— and the Sages expounded (Bereishit Rabbah 84:3):
"שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ בִּקֵּשׁ לֵישֵׁב בְּשַׁלְוָה וְכוּלֵי".
— "Jacob sought to dwell in serene tranquility, etc."
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁרָצָה בְּדַעְתוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיוּ מְתוּקָּנִים בָּזֶה כָּל תּוֹלְדוֹתָיו לְדוֹרוֹת,
— Meaning that Jacob resolved within his holy mind that all his future generations should be fully rectified,
שֶׁאַף עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר נִקְרְאוּ עַל שֵׁם יַעֲקֹב יִהְיֶה גַּם כֵּן מוּבְטָח בָּהֶם שֶׁהֵם נִכְלָלִים בַּקְּדוּשָּׁה;
— so that even the simplest folk designated by the name "Jacob" would be securely anchored within holiness;
וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי "בְּאֶרֶץ מְגוּרֵי אָבִיו" – שֶׁיְּקַבֵּל עַל עַצְמוֹ בְּחִינַת גֵּרוּת,
— and this was to be achieved through "the land of his father's sojournings (megurei)"—accepting upon himself the trial of exile/strangership (geirut),
וּבָזֶה יִהְיֶה נִשְׁלָם גְּזֵירַת "כִּי גֵר יִהְיֶה זַרְעֲךָ וְגוֹמֵר" (בְּרֵאשִׁית טו, יג).
— thereby exhausting the Covenant of the Pieces: "for your seed shall be a stranger (ger) in a land not theirs".
וּגְזֵירַת "וַעֲבָדוּם וְעִנּוּ אֹתָם" (שָׁם) – חָשַׁב בְּדַעְתוֹ שֶׁכְּבָר קִבֵּל הוּא עָלָיו בְּעַד כָּל כְּלַל זַרְעוֹ,
— And the decree of "and they shall serve them and afflict them"—Jacob reasoned that he had already endured it personally on behalf of all his future descendants,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר לְלָבָן: "עֲבַדְתִּיךָ אַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה בִּשְׁתֵּי בְנֹתֶיךָ וְשֵׁשׁ שָׁנִים בְּצֹאנֶךָ" (שָׁם לא, מא),
— just as he declared to Laban: "I served you fourteen years for your two daughters, and six years for your flock",
וְגַם הָעִינּוּי סָבַל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "הָיִיתִי בַיּוֹם אֲכָלַנִי חֹרֶב וְקֶרַח בַּלָּיְלָה וַתִּדַּד שְׁנָתִי מֵעֵינָי" (שָׁם פסוק מ);
— and affliction he had certainly endured: "Thus I was: in the day the drought consumed me, and the frost by night; and my sleep fled from my eyes";
וְעַל יְדֵי הַגֵּרוּת יִהְיֶה שְׁלֵימוּת הַבֵּירוּר בְּעַד כְּלַל נַפְשׁוֹת צֶאֱצָאָיו לְדוֹרוֹת, אֲפִילּוּ אֲשֶׁר בְּשֵׁם יַעֲקֹב יִכָּנֶה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
— so that through this final sojourning, the spiritual rectification would be completed for all his offspring, even down to the simple level of "Jacob."

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 84:3: “‘If a lash causes death suddenly’ (Job 9:23) – Antoninos asked Rabbeinu, he said to him: ‘What is the meaning of what is written: ‘If a lash causes death suddenly’?’ Rabbi (Yehuda HaNasi) said: ‘(If you were to) decree that one should receive one hundred lashes and they would give him one hundred dinars. The total of this is the total of that, but he will not get anything from him, and in that way he makes a mockery of the one receiving the lashes. ‘He mocks at the undoing of the innocent’ (Job 9:23) – Rav Aḥa said: When the righteous live in tranquility and seek to live in tranquility in this world, the accuser comes and accuses them. He says: Is what is prepared for them in the World to Come not sufficient for them, that they seek to live in tranquility in this world? Know that it is so; Jacob our patriarch, because he sought to live in tranquility in this world, was confronted by the accuser regarding Joseph. ‘I was not tranquil, was not silent’ (Job 3:26). ‘I was not tranquil’ – from Esau; ‘was not silent’ – from Laban. ‘And I did not rest’ (Job 3:26) – from Dina. ‘But turmoil came’ (Job 3:26) – the turmoil of Joseph came upon me.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash 1:1: “When Joseph told them that only Benjamin would be a slave, Judah settled it in his heart that this had not come as punishment for the sale. Rather, the very fact that Joseph was sold as a slave was brought about from Heaven, so that through him the decree of the Covenant between the Pieces, ‘and they shall serve them and afflict them,’ would be fulfilled, and specifically through Joseph, because he was the choicest among them. For we have already said that Jacob believed that the servitude and the affliction had already been fulfilled through him, in what he suffered with Laban, as he said, ‘Thus I was: by day the heat consumed me,’ and so on; and therefore Jacob sought to dwell in tranquility (as explained in Vayeshev, discourse 1). And Judah believed that Joseph had been chosen to complete the servitude and the affliction through himself.”

: “When Joseph told them that only Benjamin would be a slave, Judah settled it in his heart that this had not come as punishment for the sale. Rather, the very fact that Joseph was sold as a slave was brought about from Heaven, so that through him the decree of the Covenant between the Pieces, ‘and they shall serve them and afflict them,’ would be fulfilled, and specifically through Joseph, because he was the choicest among them. For we have already said that Jacob believed that the servitude and the affliction had already been fulfilled through him, in what he suffered with Laban, as he said, ‘Thus I was: by day the heat consumed me,’ and so on; and therefore Jacob sought to dwell in tranquility (as explained in Vayeshev, discourse 1). And Judah believed that Joseph had been chosen to complete the servitude and the affliction through himself.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Rav Tzadok himself refers back to this discourse: Jacob counted his years with Laban as the fulfilment of “they shall serve them and afflict them.” Vayigash 1 takes the reasoning one generation further. Judah reads Joseph’s sale, and then Benjamin’s threatened slavery, as Heaven completing the servitude that Jacob had believed was already finished.

p: וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "אֵלֶּה תֹּלְדוֹת יַעֲקֹב יוֹסֵף וְגוֹמֵר", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "קָפַץ עָלָיו רוּגְזוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף" (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פד, ג) –
— And upon this Scripture states: "These are the generations of Jacob: Joseph, etc.," upon which the Midrash remarks: "Immediately the ordeal of Joseph pounced upon him"—
הַיְינוּ שֶׁהֶרְאוּ לוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ עוֹד בֵּירוּרִים בְּזַרְעוֹ מַה שֶּׁצָּרִיךְ עוֹד לְתִיקּוּן,
— meaning Heaven showed him that deeper rectifications were still required within his seed,
כְּעִנְיַן הוֹצָאַת דִּבָּה שֶׁל יוֹסֵף, וְגַם עִנְיַן מְכִירַת יוֹסֵף כַּיָּדוּעַ.
— as manifest in Joseph bringing an evil report, and the subsequent selling of Joseph.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 84:3: “‘If a lash causes death suddenly’ (Job 9:23) – Antoninos asked Rabbeinu, he said to him: ‘What is the meaning of what is written: ‘If a lash causes death suddenly’?’ Rabbi (Yehuda HaNasi) said: ‘(If you were to) decree that one should receive one hundred lashes and they would give him one hundred dinars. The total of this is the total of that, but he will not get anything from him, and in that way he makes a mockery of the one receiving the lashes. ‘He mocks at the undoing of the innocent’ (Job 9:23) – Rav Aḥa said: When the righteous live in tranquility and seek to live in tranquility in this world, the accuser comes and accuses them. He says: Is what is prepared for them in the World to Come not sufficient for them, that they seek to live in tranquility in this world? Know that it is so; Jacob our patriarch, because he sought to live in tranquility in this world, was confronted by the accuser regarding Joseph. ‘I was not tranquil, was not silent’ (Job 3:26). ‘I was not tranquil’ – from Esau; ‘was not silent’ – from Laban. ‘And I did not rest’ (Job 3:26) – from Dina. ‘But turmoil came’ (Job 3:26) – the turmoil of Joseph came upon me.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Mei HaShiloach I, Vayishlach §2: “‘God ascended from upon him, in the place where He had spoken with him.’ The blessed God showed him that he still needed further clarification. … This is the meaning of ‘He ascended from upon him’: as though Jacob still needed to hold fast to Him. ‘In the place where He had spoken with him’ means that in this very matter, the matter of wealth of which the verse speaks, further clarification was required, for it was not yet complete. With this same meaning it was said of Abraham, ‘God ascended from upon Abraham,’ after the passage of circumcision: even now he still required further clarification through the trial of the Binding of Isaac. There, however, ‘in the place where He had spoken with him’ is not said, because it was not the same matter.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Mei HaShiloach reads God’s ascent as a sign that the present achievement does not complete the work of clarification. His comparison with Abraham’s circumcision followed by the Binding gives a second concrete instance of the progression that Rav Tzadok sees in Jacob’s hoped-for rest followed by Joseph’s ordeal.

p: וְאַחַר כָּךְ נֶאֱמַר: "וְיִשְׂרָאֵל אָהַב אֶת יוֹסֵף מִכָּל בָּנָיו כִּי בֶן זְקֻנִים הוּא לוֹ" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לז, ג) –
— And subsequently it is stated: "Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age (ben zekunim)":
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁחָשַׁב יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁעַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת "יִשְׂרָאֵל", דְּהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ הַתּוֹרָה, יִהְיֶה עַל כָּל פָּנִים בָּזֶה שְׁלֵימוּת הַבֵּירוּר,
— meaning our father Jacob thought that through the elevated level of "Israel"—the power of Torah—rectification would certainly be finalized,
שֶׁעַל זֶה יוֹרֶה שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל;
— as signified by the name Israel;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (קִדּוּשִׁין ל עַמּוּד ב): "בָּרָאתִי יֵצֶר הָרָע, וּבָרָאתִי לוֹ תּוֹרָה תַּבְלִין",
— as it is written: "I created the evil inclination, and I created the Torah as its antidote",
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, רב עַמּוּד א): "לֵית לָךְ מִלָּה לְמִתְבַּר יֵצֶר הָרָע אֶלָּא אוֹרַיְיתָא".
— and in the Zohar: "there is nothing to shatter the evil inclination except Torah."
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה "אָהַב אֶת יוֹסֵף מִכָּל בָּנָיו כִּי בֶן זְקֻנִים הוּא לוֹ",
— And on this account "he loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age",
וּכְתַרְגּוּם אוּנְקְלוֹס: "אֲרֵי בַּר חַכִּים הוּא לֵיהּ",
— and as Targum Onkelos translates: "for he was a wise son unto him",
וּכְמַשְׁמָעוּת תֵּיבַת "זָקֵן" – זֶ'ה קָ'נָה חָ'כְמָה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם קִדּוּשִׁין לב עַמּוּד ב),
— matching the rabbinic definition of zaken: "one who has acquired wisdom" (Kiddushin 32b),
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַחָכְמָה יֵשׁ לָהּ קִנְיָן בְּלִבּוֹ.
— meaning that wisdom had become an internalized acquisition in Joseph's heart.

paragraphs.text: Kiddushin 32b: “§ The Sages taught with regard to the verse: ‘Before the hoary head you shall stand and you shall revere the face of an elder, and you shall fear your God’ (Leviticus 19:32): One might have thought that it is obligatory to stand before a simple (ashmai) elder. Therefore, the verse states: ‘elder,’ and an ‘elder’ means nothing other than a wise man, as it is stated: ‘Gather unto Me seventy men of the Elders of Israel, whom you know to be the Elders of the people’ (Numbers 11:16). Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says: An ‘elder (zaken)’ means nothing other than one who has acquired wisdom. He interprets the word zaken as a contraction of the phrase zeh kanna, meaning: This one has acquired. Elsewhere the word kanna is used in reference to wisdom, as it is stated that wisdom says: ‘The Lord acquired me (kanani) at the beginning of His way’ (Proverbs 8:22).”

h: Torah and the Mission to Shechem

p: וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר אַחַר זֶה: "וַיֹּאמֶר יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל יוֹסֵף: הֲלוֹא אַחֶיךָ רֹעִים בִּשְׁכֶם, לְכָה וְאֶשְׁלָחֲךָ אֲלֵיהֶם" (שָׁם פסוק יג) –
— And concerning this it is stated immediately following: "And Israel said unto Joseph: Do not your brothers feed the flock in Shechem? Come (lekhah), and I will send you unto them":
הַיְינוּ מִצַּד בְּחִינַת "יִשְׂרָאֵל" אָמַר אֶל יוֹסֵף: שֶׁהוּא בְּכֹחַ הַתּוֹרָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל יְתַקֵּן אֶת הַקִּלְקוּל אֲשֶׁר בִּשְׁכֶם,
— from the vantage of "Israel" he dispatched Joseph: that through the power of Torah, Joseph should rectify the breach at Shechem,
שֶׁהוּא הַמָּקוֹם הַמּוּכָן לְפוּרְעָנוּת שֶׁשָּׁם נִפְרְצָה הָעֶרְוָה (בְּדִינָה).
— which was the territory primed for tragedy where sexual boundaries were breached with Dinah.
וְזֶהוּ "לְכָה וְאֶשְׁלָחֲךָ", שֶׁתֵּיבַת "לְכָה" נִרְאֶה כִּמְיוּתָּר;
— And this is the emphasis of "Come (lekhah)," where the word appears grammatically redundant;
רַק הָרֶמֶז הוּא שֶׁזֶּה הַדָּבָר הַנּוֹגֵעַ לְךָ דַּוְוקָא, שֶׁבְּכֹחֲךָ לְתַקֵּן.
— hinting that this mission pertained uniquely to Joseph, who possessed the specific spiritual power of the Covenant to repair it.
וְעַל זֶה יוֹרֶה גַּם אוֹת הֵ"א הַמְּיוּתָּר ("לְכָה" תַּחַת "לֵךְ"),
— And to this alludes the additional letter Hei in lekhah (לְכָה) rather than lekh (לֵךְ),
הַמְּרַמֵּז לִכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
— alluding to Knesset Yisrael (the final Hei of the Tetragrammaton),
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁלְּךָ תּוּכַל לְתַקֵּן כְּלַל נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
— that through his Torah he might rectify the collective souls of Israel.

paragraphs.text: Connection: Rashi is the source of Rav Tzadok’s phrase “the place prepared for calamity,” and he names the same three events: Dinah, the sale of Joseph, and the split of the Davidic kingdom. In the same comment he also ties Joseph’s mission to the decree “your seed shall be strangers,” which links Rav Tzadok’s theme of geirut (3.5–3.6) to the mission to Shechem.

p: וְגַם בָּזֶה הֶרְאוּ לוֹ שֶׁאֵין עוֹד תַּכְלִית הַבֵּירוּר בִּשְׁלֵימוּת,
— Yet in this too Heaven showed Jacob that the final rectification was not yet at hand,
כִּי עַל יְדֵי שְׁלִיחוּת זֶה בִּשְׁכֶם מָכְרוּ אֶת יוֹסֵף,
— for through this very mission to Shechem the brothers sold Joseph,
שֶׁזֶּה הוּא גַּם כֵּן מֵעֵין פְּגַם הַבְּרִית,
— which is also akin to a blemish of the covenant,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "עַל מִכְרָם בַּכֶּסֶף צַדִּיק" (עָמוֹס ב, ו).
— as it is written: "because they sold the righteous (tzaddik) for silver" (Amos 2:6).
וְגַם בִּשְׁכֶם נֶחְלְקָה מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד (מְלָכִים א יב),
— Furthermore, at Shechem the Davidic monarchy was split,
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן שַׁיָּיכוּת לָזֶה, שֶׁהָיָה עַל יְדֵי יָרָבְעָם בֶּן נְבָט שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ גַּם כֵּן כֹּחַ הַתּוֹרָה,
— which directly relates to this, occurring through Jeroboam son of Nebat who also possessed immense Torah power,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סַנְהֶדְרִין קב עַמּוּד א):
— as written in Sanhedrin (102a):
עַל פָּסוּק "שְׁנֵיהֶם לְבַדָּם בַּשָּׂדֶה" (מְלָכִים א יא, כט) – שֶׁכָּל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים דּוֹמִין לִפְנֵיהֶם כְּעִשְׂבֵּי הַשָּׂדֶה;
— on "and they two were alone in the field"—that all contemporary Torah scholars appeared before them like grass of the field;
וְעַל פָּסוּק: "וְהוּא מִתְכַּסֶּה בְּשַׂלְמָה חֲדָשָׁה" (שָׁם) – שֶׁתּוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל יָרָבְעָם לֹא הָיָה בָּהּ שׁוּם דֹּפִי כְּשַׂלְמָה חֲדָשָׁה.
— and on "and he had clad himself with a new garment"—that Jeroboam's Torah was flawless like a pristine new garment.
וְשָׁמַעְנוּ מֵרַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא:
— And we heard from our Holy Master of blessed memory:
שֶׁעֲבוּר זֶה הָיָה לוֹ חֵן לְיָרָבְעָם בְּעֵינֵי אֲחִיָּה הַשִּׁילוֹנִי,
— that for this reason Jeroboam found grace in the eyes of Ahijah the Shilonite,
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיָה יָרָבְעָם מְנוּקֶּה מִתַּאֲווֹת,
— because Jeroboam was initially thoroughly cleansed of physical lusts,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ "אֶפְרָתִי" (שָׁם פסוק כו) שֶׁמּוֹרֶה עַל זֶה,
— as indicated by his lineage titled "Ephrathite",
וַאֲחִיָּה הָיָה מִשִּׁילֹה שֶׁהוּא מֵחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף.
— and Ahijah hailed from Shiloh, the tribal portion of Joseph.
וְכֵן בֶּאֱמֶת יָצָא מִמֶּנּוּ מְשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף – מֵאֲבִיָּה בֶּן יָרָבְעָם,
— And indeed, from Jeroboam's line Mashiach ben Yosef is destined to issue through his righteous son Aviyah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּזֹהַר חָדָשׁ בָּלָק נו עַמּוּד א),
— as written in Zohar Chadash (Balak 56a),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ: "יַעַן נִמְצָא בוֹ דָּבָר טוֹב" (מְלָכִים א יד, יג).
— as Scripture testifies of him: "because in him there is found some good thing toward Hashem".

p: וְהֶרְאוּ לוֹ שֶׁגַּם בָּזֶה אֵין תַּכְלִית הַבֵּירוּר עוֹד,
— Yet Heaven demonstrated to Jacob that even here lay not the ultimate completion,
כִּדְאִיתָא בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פד, יט) עַל פָּסוּק: "הִנֵּה בַּעַל הַחֲלֹמוֹת הַלָּזֶה בָּא" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לז, יט) –
— as taught in Bereishit Rabbah (84:19) on "Behold, this dreamer comes"—
זֶה עָתִיד לְהַשִּׂיאׇם לִבְעָלִים,
— saying: this line will cause Israel to worship the Baalim,
וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי עֶגְלֵי יָרָבְעָם (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמַתְּנוֹת כְּהֻנָּה).
— which occurred through the golden calves of Jeroboam (Matnot Kehunah).
כִּי גַּם עַל יְדֵי מְשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף לֹא תִּהְיֶה הַגְּאוּלָּה בִּשְׁלֵימוּת,
— For even through Mashiach ben Yosef the redemption is not finalized,
רַק דַּוְוקָא עַל יְדֵי מְשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד:
— rather it culminates exclusively through Mashiach ben David:

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Ne’os Deshe I (R. Shmuel Dov Asher Leiner), Vayeshev, p. 21 (Piotrkow, 1908): “Yehudah’s quality is the opposite of Yosef’s quality. Yosef’s quality is to be strict with himself, to avoid entering uncertainty, and to overcome his inclination, as it is written, ‘I fear God.’ This is very good, but it cannot rise to a great level. Yehudah’s quality is to enter uncertainty, as with Yehudah and Tamar, and David and Bathsheba. … But when a heavenly voice declared, ‘From Me these hidden matters proceeded,’ Yehudah then merited kingship; the Holy One could bestow no greater good. This requires understanding.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: This passage distinguishes the spiritual work of Yosef from that of Yehudah, from whom David descends. It helps explain why the present discourse assigns the completion of redemption to the son of David: guarded purity does not encompass the same work as a trial whose hidden purpose is disclosed afterward. The passage makes the vindication depend on the heavenly declaration.
